text: I. Professional Core PositioningThe core focus is on "researching the design, manufacturing, operation laws, and intelligent upgrading of mechanical systems", concentrating on converting natural science principles into practical mechanical equipment and technologies, addressing issues ranging from micro-components to large-scale complex mechanical systems in terms of research, production, and control, and serving almost all industrial sectors such as aerospace, automotive manufacturing, energy equipment, and intelligent manufacturing.II. Training ObjectivesTo cultivate comprehensive engineering technical talents with a solid foundation in mechanical engineering theory, strong engineering practice capabilities, and innovative thinking, who can engage in scientific research, technology development, engineering design, production management, etc. in fields such as mechanical design, manufacturing automation, mechatronics, and intelligent equipment. Specific requirements include: Master the principles of modeling, analysis, design and manufacturing of mechanical systems;Have the ability to develop mechanical products throughout the entire process from concept design to production implementation;Be familiar with cutting-edge technologies such as automation control, robot technology, and digital manufacturing;Be able to solve practical problems by using tools such as computer-aided design (CAD), simulation analysis (CAE), and manufacturing (CAM);Have the ability to collaborate across disciplines and be able to adapt to the upgrading needs of industries such as intelligent manufacturing and green manufacturing.
